oneliner.t: Retired Marine (20 years combined Navy and Marine Corps service) and former congressional veteran-services staffer, the Democratic nominee in toss-up AZ-06, unopposed in her primary, and the race's top fundraiser through July 1, 2026.

hometown.t: Pinal County, Arizona (raised in a farmworker family)

profile.residence: Tucson area, AZ (campaign mailing address in Marana; owns a Tucson rental property)

upbringing.t: Born in Florence and raised in a farmworker family in rural Pinal County; she says the family relied on food assistance and AHCCCS and that she worked in cotton fields as a child. She joined the Navy at 17 (1994–1997), then the Marine Corps (1998–2016), serving as a drill instructor with deployments to Iraq and Afghanistan. After retiring she earned a bachelor's (American Military University, 2013) and master's (Grand Canyon University, 2019), worked in veterans outreach and nonprofits, and was a veteran services representative for Rep. Tom O'Halleran. She ran for the Arizona Senate in 2020 and lost. She is a single mother of a son.

profile.office_note: Her 2020 survey says she was appointed to the governing board of a small rural school district in Red Rock; title and dates not documented, so not counted.

career.role: Marine (incl. drill instructor; Iraq and Afghanistan deployments; retired)

career.org: Pima Community College; A Place Called Home

career.role: Founder; consulting clients incl. campaigns, Keep Courts Accountable PAC, Americans for Contraception, VetsForward

platform.t: Tackle the cost of food, gas, housing and child care; reverse 'billionaire tax breaks' in H.R. 1, end tariffs and restore SNAP funding.
Reverse the 2025 SNAP and Medicaid changes, citing her family's reliance on food aid and AHCCCS and the risk to rural hospitals.
'Safe Communities, Strong Borders & Real Immigration Solutions'; criticized DHS tactics in the Minneapolis enforcement surge.
Says the administration went to war without a plan, goals or exit strategy, but opposes simply pulling troops out.
Stop 'unfair price disparities in rural communities' and strengthen consumer protections.
Veterans, water/climate for rural Arizona, government accountability and national security are listed priorities (issue pages not opened).

promises.t: Hold town halls again within her first 100 days.
Work to reverse H.R. 1's SNAP and Medicaid changes.
Work with Democrats, Republicans and Independents.

claims.claim: Served 20 years in uniform, joining the Navy at 17 and then the Marine Corps.

record.t: Ballotpedia lists Navy 1994–1997 and Marine Corps 1998–2016 (about 21 years combined). Age at enlistment not independently documented.

Ballotpedia lists two Iraq tours and one Afghanistan tour (sourced to her own survey). A Breitbart report citing Navy records says she did not deploy overseas in 1994–1997, which does not conflict with Marine Corps deployments. Service records were not opened.

networth.note: Assets minus liabilities from the 2026 candidate report (to May 15, 2026); matches the Copper Courier calculation.

note.t: Assets: Tucson rental property ($250K–$500K), Radar Strategies stake ($50K–$100K, forfeited April 2025), 529 plan for her son, and a nominal stake in her firm Poderoza Strategies. Income: military retired pay (~$34.7K), VA disability, rent, campaign salary. Liabilities: mortgage ($250K–$500K), student loans, credit cards and home-improvement loans. Her original 2025 report listed the Radar stake at $1M–$5M and omitted the rental property; she amended it in mid-2026 after the Free Beacon reported the original figure. House Ethics guidance treats amendments as the normal correction route (Copper Courier). Positions: board of VetsForward; AZ Attorney General's Veterans & Military Advisory Council; earlier boards of Arizona Democratic Women and Children's Action Alliance; Arizona chair of Vote Mama.

legal.t: Her 2025 House candidate financial disclosure valued her stake in her consulting firm, Radar Strategies, at $1M–$5M and omitted a rental property; she filed an amendment revaluing the stake at $50K–$100K. Her amended filing (signed July 1, 2026) and her 2026 report list the stake at $50,001–$100,000; the campaign said she listed the firm's total value instead of her share. The amendment also added a Tucson rental property ($250K–$500K) omitted from the original.

research_notes: DISCLOSURE: both a conservative outlet (Free Beacon) and a progressive outlet (Copper Courier) documented the original $1M–$5M entry and its amendment, so the facts are cross-corroborated; the 'millionaire' characterization is not supported by her corrected filings. PERSONAL: Breitbart (Jul 9, 2026), citing the Daily Mail, reported a 1998 marriage abroad that lasted 16 days and a 2001 default divorce; the campaign called it 'one short chapter' ending nearly 30 years ago. No court record was opened and only one reporting chain exists, so it is excluded from scored fields; it is not a foreign-government or foreign-business tie. Ciscomani's debate allegations (lobbying ties, not paying her own taxes, 'defund the police' endorsers) are opponent claims and were not substantiated in sources opened. Photo not retrieved.
